Prevention: Carry out soil testing before fertilizer application.
Boost crop health by applying the recommnded fertilizers and manure.
East-West orientation to receive maximum light to enhance quality of polllen quality.
Plant more flowering plants around the ochard to attract bees.
Keep the field weed free to ease nutrient competition.
Avoid excess use of chemical sprays especially at flowering so as not to kill pollinators.
Intercrop with trap crops e.g. carrots, cucurbits, kales, spider plant.
Monitoring: Dry scars of floral stalk remains on the vine with no small fruits attached.
Presence of thrips (minute slender dark brown insects with fringed wings).
Take action when 5% of the flowers are aborted in 100 plants.
Direct Control (Non-chemical): Milla fertilizer at planting at the rate of 100g/tree in two splits (N,P,K,B:15,9,20,0.02).
Spray foliar feed with boron nutrient e.g.
Solubor at the rate 50-60g/20litres of water or
Easygro-flowers-30-40g/20l before and during flowering and at fruiting stages at fortnight interval.
Put up at least one beehive near the ochard, bees are the best insect pollinators.
Carry out hand pollination using a paint brush.
Spray alpha naphthalene acetic acid before flowering e.g.
Plantone at exactly 4mls/20 litres of water.
Spray 2 spoonfuls of mild detergent (tepeal) in 5 litres of water to control thrips.
Direct Control (Chemical): When using a pesticide always wear protective equipment.
Follow the instructions on the product label, such as dosage, timing of application, max number of sprays, restricted re
Always consult recent list of registered pesticides (PCPB).
In case of presence of thrips during flowering, spray alphacypermethrin (Albaz 10
EC, Alfatox 10% EC, Alphacymba 10% EC at 5ml/20litres of water)
EC at 10-15mls in 20 litres of water, Keshet 2.5
EC at 15mls in 20 litres of water)
